kind: assumptions and analysis choices; nothing in this file is measured by this fixture in the Demerzel repository (deleted_triggers repeats counts that PSY-009 takes from the repository history)

variance.note: Used everywhere: daily counts, window totals, control logs and the transfer task. The population variance (divisor n) is never reported.

day_definition.note: A day is the UTC date of the event's timestamp (offset 0). The other offsets add that many hours before the date is taken, which moves the day boundary; they test whether the conclusion depends on the boundary and are nobody's time zone.

claimed_rate.note: The description under test, taken from the mean rounded to a whole number. A day 'looks like the claim' when its count lies within the tolerance of the value.

quantile_rule: nearest rank: the level-p quantile of n values is the k-th smallest with k = ceil(p * n / 100)

poisson_benchmark.note: A Poisson distribution whose mean is the observed mean per calendar day. It is a benchmark for 'events arrive independently at a constant rate', not a model fitted and compared with others (PSY-022 does that).

anti_pattern_rule.note: Copied by hand from the detection sentence of the pattern record; analyze.py checks that the sentence in the snapshot still contains this threshold.

episode_note: Analysis choice: burst days at most this many days apart belong to one episode.

windows.note: Blocks of consecutive days counted from the first day of the log, not calendar weeks. Each length must divide the number of calendar days.

deleted_triggers.note: Not read by this fixture, which reads the files present at the pinned commit and not the repository history. PSY-009 reports that twelve trigger files were deleted from the repository without being archived; `git log --diff-filter=D --name-only 4b03838800dcd4894f1e026461979bff1d985ca8 -- state/triggers/` lists them. The days are the dates in the deleted file names. One of the seven dated 2026-03-20 has the type self_initiated, which the producer workflow does not write; all twelve are added, the larger change. analyze.py uses them for the sensitivity section deleted_triggers and for nothing else.

controls.note: Synthetic logs with the observed number of events and days, used to show that the code can return a small index of dispersion. 'even' spreads the events as evenly as possible; 'constant_rate' places each event on a day drawn uniformly with random.Random(seed).random(); 'planted_burst' adds events to one day of the even log.

transfer_task.note: Hypothetical log of incoming webhooks for the learner task. Not Streeling data and not a forecast.
